_doc: The numbers of the reactor, warp, damage control and officers (src/Core/Data/SystemsDef.Reactor.cs reads them), from the battle console mockup (REACTOR, WARP, REPAIR, REPAIR_JOBS, OFFICER, ROSTER; openspec/changes/reactor, warp, damage-control, officers). Temperatures are percent of the core's limit; a share is a fraction of 1. A missing key takes the code default, which is the mockup's number.

reactor._doc: Cooling and loop hits tuned 2026-11-11 (owner: "yea fix it", of small ships melting down once one coolant loop was hit, at about 78 % hull): cool_per_flow 0.04 to 0.06, hit.loop_p 0.18 to 0.12, so one loop lost leaves the core near 67 % and a meltdown needs both. Magnetic confinement coils lose alignment while the confinement (the reactor subsystem's health) is damaged; misalignment cuts the output by efficiency_loss of the mean offset and adds heat. Coolant loops' pumps draw flow_e a point of flow; they carry heat away in proportion to the core temperature. Coolant offline, or the core at critical_pct, for meltdown_s and the reactor explodes, blast_dmg falling to 0 at blast_km.

hit._doc: What a hit through the shields may do to the reactor and the warp drive: knock a coil out of alignment by up to coil_knock (and the confinement down by conf_per_dmg a point of damage), damage a coolant loop by loop_dmg plus up to loop_dmg_rand, or a nacelle by nacelle_dmg.

warp._doc: The energy put into warp is split between the nacelles still working, which charge the banks at charge_k of what they draw times their health. A jump needs jump_e in the banks (of bank_e). An armed drive takes the reactor's free energy, up to coil_e, and gives way first when the systems need more than the output. A course is plotted over plot_s, slowed by damaged sensors, stopped when they are out. Coolant leaks from damaged loops at leak_per_s; a jump spends coolant_jump. Above qg_block a jump needs the safety override. The jump risk is 1 less the product of (1 less each factor's risk), and the jump rolls against that same number. A jump streaks away at out_speed_m_s for out_s. A withdrawal (the menu's Withdraw) jumps by itself only while the risk is at or under withdraw_max_risk; over it, the drive holds and says why, and the captain may still jump by hand from the Warp page or call the withdrawal off with Withdraw again. A withdrawal whose drive can no longer charge (every nacelle wrecked, the banks short) is called off by itself.

mishap._doc: A failed jump, scaled by the risk and a severity roll: each nacelle loses (nacelle + nacelle_sev x severity) x risk x nacelle_x, the coolant coolant_sev x severity, the hull hull_dmg + hull_dmg_sev x risk x severity; banks and course are lost. Past breach_risk with a severity past breach_sev the core breaches.

repair._doc: Damage control: the crews, one for each point of repair energy, work down the captain's queue, at most max_crews on one job, the rest on the next job that needs them. A crew mends tuning.json's repair_per_e_s of a job's health a second (the weapon mounts mount_repair_per_e_s), browned out with the rest of the ship. jobs: id, name, icon, the short name the docked page uses; queue: the order a ship starts with.

officers._doc: Each station has one slot. An officer has a rank (0-3), a specialty (the station trained for) and a skill from 1 (Green) to 4 (Legend); in a slot of their own specialty they count their whole skill, anywhere else half of it, rounded down. Each ability, per skill level, is read by its rule. The roster is the player's side's officers (every ship of it that is not a station has its own): id, name, rank, specialty, skill. names and ranks rename them by faction (ids and every rule the same); a second ship of a faction takes the names shifted by name_shift.
